results.summary_before: This design is a 40-bit shift register with a hardcoded secret number, forming a challenge where the output goes high only when the correct 40-bit sequence is shifted in. The user shifts bits in serially, one per clock cycle, and after 40 bits the output indicates whether the sequence matches. The register acts as a sliding window, so every new bit checks a new candidate. No external hardware is required beyond the clock, reset, and two input pins.

results.summary_before: This chip is an SPI-controlled 8-channel LED driver with a 16-register file, where eight BRIGHT registers set the PWM brightness of eight LED outputs. Each SPI transaction is 16 bits, with the first byte selecting a register address and direction and the second byte carrying data, and the PWM uses a shared 8-bit counter with a prescaler for flicker-free refresh. It is tested through a recommended bring-up sequence that verifies SPI communication, address decoding, read/write loopback, read-only protection, enable control, and LED output. The design requires a Pmod 8LD with eight discrete LEDs connected to the output Pmod header, and is notable for its robust SPI interface with synchronizers and a clear register map.

results.summary_before: This design implements a colorful version of the 2048 sliding tile puzzle game. It outputs a VGA video signal and accepts directional inputs from a keyboard or game controller to move the tiles. The design is intended to be run on an FPGA, such as the Tiny Tapeout FPGA, and requires a VGA display and input device. It was successfully tested on the TT FPGA with a game pmod, and a VGA playground link is provided for simulation.

results.summary_before: This project implements a simple bandgap reference that outputs a stable voltage over a temperature range of -40°C to 125°C, with about 1% variation in simulation. It lacks supply noise rejection and trimming, making it a basic design for providing a stable reference. Testing requires applying 3.3V to the analog supply and measuring the output voltage over temperature using a bench power supply, multimeter, thermocouple, and temperature chamber. The documentation includes a simulation graph showing the typical output voltage range.

results.notes: Removed machine-learning because the source describes statistical event classification, not ML hardware; added instrumentation for the sensor measurement/classification role.
results.summary_before: This Verilog design is a zero-RAM streaming statistical co-processor that tracks a median and median absolute deviation baseline from an 8-bit input stream and classifies events using a temporal persistence engine. It outputs the tracked baseline on the eight outputs and an event code on three bidirectional pins, with a wake interrupt and debug and configuration pins. It is tested by applying an 8-bit signal and configuration pins, then injecting a one-cycle spike, a permanent baseline jump, a slow ramp, or a held value to obtain the corresponding glitch, shift, drift or stuck-sensor codes. The design is notable for distinguishing transient outliers from persistent baseline shifts without any memory buffers.

results.summary_before: This is a pipelined 50 MHz byte-stream int8 multiply-accumulate engine with a single int32 accumulator, a streaming vector-MAC primitive, a wide-input mode, and a SPILL opcode for reading raw accumulator values. It also includes a MISR self-test and a serial debug interface, and is intended as a hardware target for a compiler/MLIR backend. The design is verified with a cocotb testbench that includes directed tests, randomized differential testing against a Python model, and an exhaustive test of the Booth multiplier. No external hardware is required; the host microcontroller drives the pins to feed instructions and operands and read results.
